content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate downward corrections after strong upward moves; model fails to recognize mean reversion in sentiment-driven declines.
- When sentiment is negative (or low), model consistently overcorrects downward, leading to underestimation of true price.
- When sentiment is positive (or high), model overestimates upside potential, especially in early forecast periods.
- Model exhibits lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — delays in adjusting forecasts when sentiment turns sharply.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage price surges (last 5–7 days) unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is volatile or oscillating, model tends to smooth out extremes, leading to underprediction of volatility-driven moves.
- Model overweights recent price action in forecasting, ignoring sentiment context — especially when sentiment is weak or mixed.
